source: Opinion: Do not close the Fenwick Bridge on the strength of one report. Mayor Quintrell announced the closure on Monday, and she leaned entirely on the inspection: “The inspection was unambiguous — the firm wrote that ‘the east pier cannot be certified for another season,’ and I will not gamble with a school bus route.” That sentence deserves a second look. The firm that wrote it, Calder & Voss, is one of three bidders on the replacement contract, a fact the mayor’s statement did not mention. A firm that profits from a replacement has every incentive to read a crack as a crisis. The bridge carried its full load through last winter without incident. Before the town spends four years and a detour on the mayor’s reading of one paragraph, it should commission an independent inspection from a firm with no bid on the table. If that inspection says close it, close it.

The columnist's claim about the firm's incentive is reported as the columnist's argument, not as a finding about the firm.
